title: Empress Tree: Old Paulownias You Can Visit
meta_description: A fast Chinese tree with violet spring flowers. Milan's grew on a wartime bomb site in Brera, and residents saved it from a building plot in 2016.
intro: The empress tree, Paulownia tomentosa, is a native of China named after Anna Pavlovna, the Russian grand duchess who became queen of the Netherlands. It grows famously fast and in spring carries upright sprays of violet flowers before the leaves come. Milan's grew by itself on a Brera corner left empty after wartime bombing, and when a developer held the right to build there, a residents' committee persuaded the city to take the 155 square metre plot in 2016. On Staten Island, NYC Parks measured the one at Snug Harbor in 1985 at about 5.2 metres round, with leaves that can reach a foot across. In Bratislava, two sources give the paulownia in Škarniclova Park ages ninety years apart, sixty and a hundred and fifty, and both stand. East Hampton's came from a reader, who photographed the label on its trunk.
